notes.text: Jonathan Marchessault is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward.
Daemon Hunt joined from MIN on Oct 25 and has played beside Jayden Struble.

Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.

LAK.head: The Kings have a lot going for them
LAK.body: Even though Los Angeles will be without Fiala, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Predators’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Haula meets his old team
paras: The Kings (5-7-2) beat San Jose 7-2 on Wednesday, and the Predators have won three straight. Going in, the Preds are fifth in the Central (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (tied for 28th).

The Predators’ record (.594) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.525), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Kings have played better than their record (.429) says: their chances are worth about .613, mostly because they’re 2-5 in one-goal games.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (31st), so the Kings are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. As for the Kings, they leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (3rd) and lean hard on their top players (4th lowest). The Kings have the edge over the Predators on forecheck pressure.

Filip Forsberg (5 G / 14 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Steven Stamkos (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Adrian Kempe (6 G / 6 A / 12 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind.

Nashville has two options in net: Juuse Saros (4-3-4 / .908 SV% in 11 GS) and Justus Annunen (3-1-0 / .873 SV% in 4 GS). Saros has started six of their last ten games, but Annunen got the last one on Thursday. Los Angeles also has two options: Darcy Kuemper (5-3-1 / .885 SV% in 9 GS) and Anton Forsberg (0-4-1 / .902 SV% in 5 GS). Kuemper has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday. For both teams, it’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
